Subject: Catalyst3B - initial notice: elevated 5xx/timeouts

Sara / Acme ops team,

I wanted to let you know we're seeing elevated 5xx and timeout errors from model Catalyst3B (v2027-07-12-quant) affecting requests with longer context windows (>8k tokens) in the us-west region. Impact started ~08:50 PDT and we've observed increased error rates for streaming generation and chunked chat requests.

What we're doing now:
- Engaged inference runtime (Ben) to triage kernel/runtime failures and check KV cache behavior.
- Routing policy: temporarily moving traffic to Catalyst3B-compat (a larger memory variant) for customers that opted into fallback routing.
- Increasing request timeouts for in-flight requests to reduce client-side timeouts while we investigate.

Attachments: error snippets and node dump included (catalyst3b-error-snippets-15aug.txt, node-kernel-dump-15aug.tar.gz).

Short ask: Can you confirm if Acme is currently using long context sessions for batch scoring or streaming chat flows? That will help prioritize rollback vs targeted routing.

I'll send updates every 60 minutes or sooner if we have a mitigation. Sorry for the disruption — working to stabilize ASAP.

Thanks,

Lauren / team,

Quick triage notes from the runtime side:
- Symptom: KV cache invalidation exceptions followed by segmentation faults inside the quantized attention kernel. Manifested under long-context (>8k) generation when the model hits the FP16 fused-kernel path.
- Probable trigger: A kernel scheduling change pushed in the July release that selects a new fused attention kernel when estimated sequence length >4k and quantization profile = v2. Small fraction of nodes started crashing and causing 5xxs downstream.
- Immediate mitigation applied: rolled routing for affected nodes back to the older kernel (kernel-v1-fused) and rebalanced the job queue. This reduced error rate from ~7.2% -> ~0.9% on canary nodes.
- Action items: collect heap/kv traces for the failing nodes and roll a staged rollback for all US-west nodes hosting Catalyst3B v2027-07-12-quant.

I'll coordinate the rollout; ETA for full US-west rollback ~2.5 hours pending validations. We'll keep fallback routing in place during the window.

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Catalyst3B - recovery summary, root cause, and next steps

Sara / Acme ops,

Following up with a short post-incident summary and next steps. Thanks for your patience; full engineering RCA is linked below.

What happened (summary):
- On 2027-08-15 08:50 PDT we observed an uptick in 5xx/timeouts originating from Catalyst3B (v2027-07-12-quant) serving long-context requests.
- Root cause: a staged kernel selection change (July release) caused an incompatible fused FP16 attention kernel (kernel-v2-fused) to be selected for large sequence lengths when quantization profile = v2. The kernel path exposed a rare race in KV cache eviction that led to memory corruption and downstream 5xxs.

What we did (mitigation and recovery):
- Immediately routed affected customers to Catalyst3B-compat to preserve availability while we triaged. We kept this as a rolling fallback for customers who accepted compatibility routing.
- Rolled kernel selection back to the prior stable kernel (kernel-v1-fused) across US-west serving nodes over a staged 3-hour rollout.
- Replayed failing requests on canary nodes to validate fixes. Error rate returned to baseline (~0.2%) after rollback.
- Collected and preserved node-level dumps and KV traces; artifacts attached and available on the internal ticket.

Customer impact:
- Acme Analytics: saw intermittent 5xxs on long-context batch jobs and streaming chat between 08:50–12:15 PDT on 2027-08-15. The majority of batch scoring retried/failed; estimated ~3.8% of scoring jobs failed and were retried by Acme's job runner.
- No evidence of data leakage or retention policy violations. All logs and request bodies are intact and were preserved for audit.

Next steps and mitigations (planned):
- Engineering will remove the kernel-v2-fused auto-selection rule and add explicit compatibility checks for quantization profiles by 2027-08-22.
- We'll add additional KV cache instrumentation and a diagnostic mode customers can opt into for premium tiers.
- Postmortem doc and follow-up action items are tracked at RW-INF-4321 (link above). Expect an RFC for long-context kernel gating next week.

If Acme would like, we can schedule a 30-minute call to review the artifact bundle and the validation steps we ran. Suggest Friday 08/20 10:00 PDT — I can set up if that works.

Apologies again — we know availability is critical and we're treating this with top priority.

Best,
